annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in own graveyard. This exiles it, puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf), and grants Walking Ballista's activated abilities to all creatures with +1/+1 counters. Then consider casting Badgermole Cub with remaining mana, and proceed to combat.

annotations.description: With only 2 lands on turn 5, Archon of Cruelty (8 mana) is essentially uncastable from hand. Discarding it would be better since it could potentially be reanimated via Emperor of Bones (exile from graveyard, then put onto battlefield). Thoughtseize at 1 mana is immediately castable and can disrupt the opponent's plans, which is critical when this far behind on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Thoughtseize
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty - it's uncastable from hand with 2 lands, and putting it in the graveyard actually enables Emperor of Bones reanimation. Thoughtseize is a cheap, impactful spell that could be cast next turn.

annotations.description: The reasoning dismisses activating Agatha's Soul Cauldron when Walking Ballista is in the graveyard. Exiling Walking Ballista with Cauldron is a key combo piece in this archetype - it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal damage and pay 4 to add counters. With Young Wolf (which gets a +1/+1 counter from undying) this creates significant value. The Cauldron activation should be done before or alongside deploying Badgermole Cub.
annotations.actionTaken: Dismissed Agatha's Soul Cauldron activation as offering no immediate benefit, likely prioritizing Badgermole Cub cast instead
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in graveyard, putting the +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf or another creature, then cast Badgermole Cub. This sets up the Ballista abilities on countered creatures for future turns.

annotations.actionTaken: Activated Spymaster's Vault for connive 0, accomplishing nothing while spending mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from the graveyard, giving its activated abilities to creatures with +1/+1 counters (like Young Wolf after it dies and returns with undying). This is the core combo line of the deck. Alternatively, cast Badgermole Cub to develop the board.

annotations.description: Missed infinite damage combo. Agatha's Soul Cauldron can exile Walking Ballista from graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf. Young Wolf then has Walking Ballista's 'Remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability. Remove the counter, Young Wolf becomes 1/1, ping for 1. Then remove another... actually Young Wolf dies as a 0/0 when counter is removed, undying triggers (no +1/+1 counters), returns with a +1/+1 counter, repeat for infinite damage = lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Appeared to dismiss the Agatha's Soul Cauldron activation and likely cast Badgermole Cub instead.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in graveyard, put the +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf. Then use the Walking Ballista 'remove counter to deal 1 damage' ability repeatedly with Young Wolf's undying for infinite damage, winning the game on the spot.

annotations.description: Should have activated Agatha's Soul Cauldron first to exile Walking Ballista from the graveyard before casting Badgermole Cub. Exiling Ballista puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf) and grants it Walking Ballista's ping ability immediately. This costs no mana (just a tap) and doesn't prevent casting Badgermole Cub afterward with the remaining lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Badgermole Cub first without activating Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the graveyard first, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf (giving it Ballista's ping ability), then cast Badgermole Cub with remaining mana.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron's tap ability, which would exile a card from a graveyard (such as Walking Ballista from their own graveyard) and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature they control. This is a pure-upside activated ability that costs nothing but a tap. Exiling Walking Ballista with Agatha's Soul Cauldron is particularly powerful because it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal damage — a key combo piece in the Agatha's Soul Cauldron deck. The player also declined to cast the second copy of Agatha's Soul Cauldron, which while legendary (so they can't have two), they could have at least activated the one on the battlefield. The reasoning given was nonsensical frustration rather than strategic thinking.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Agatha's Soul Cauldron or casting any spell.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the graveyard, exile it, and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf or Delighted Halfling). This enables the Walking Ballista ping ability on that creature, which is the core combo of the deck.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge has Endurance (3/4) available to attack alongside Young Wolf, but only sends the Young Wolf. The opponent has only 14 life and an empty board (just two lands), so there's no risk of unfavorable blocks. Attacking with both Young Wolf and Endurance would deal 4 damage instead of 1, representing significant pressure. The Endurance has no summoning sickness issues (it's listed as an available attacker), and leaving it back serves no defensive purpose against an opponent with an empty board.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Young Wolf (1/1) for 1 damage, holding back Endurance (3/4)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Young Wolf and Endurance for 4 total damage. With the opponent at 14 life and no creatures on board, there's no reason to hold back the 3/4 creature.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista is in the graveyard and Agatha's Soul Cauldron is on the battlefield untapped. Exiling Walking Ballista with the Cauldron would put a +1/+1 counter on a creature AND give that creature Walking Ballista's activated abilities (remove counter to deal 1 damage, pay {4} to add a counter). This is a powerful combo interaction that was available and apparently ignored.
annotations.actionTaken: Dismissed the Agatha's Soul Cauldron activation as worthless, likely passing without using it.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf or Delighted Halfling), giving it Walking Ballista's ping and counter-adding abilities.

annotations.description: Discarding Emperor of Bones to Faithless Looting is suboptimal. Emperor of Bones is a strong 2-mana creature that can be cast from hand with the available mana (Steam Vents + Island can't cast it since it costs {1}{B}, but Steam Vents produces U or R, not B). However, looking more carefully at the mana - Steam Vents produces U/R and Island produces U, so Emperor of Bones ({1}{B}) can't be cast yet anyway. But the player has Bloodstained Mire in hand which can fetch a Swamp to enable B mana. Archon of Cruelty is the best discard target since it costs 8 mana and is essentially uncastable - it's a reanimation target but there's no reanimation in hand. The second discard of Emperor of Bones over Archon is questionable since Emperor of Bones is a cheap, playable card that provides graveyard interaction (exiling cards from opponent's graveyard which is relevant against the Soul Cauldron deck), while Archon of Cruelty is extremely expensive and unlikely to be cast normally.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Emperor of Bones as first of two cards for Faithless Looting
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty and one of the duplicate cards (like the second Psychic Frog or second Emperor of Bones), keeping more castable threats. Archon of Cruelty at 8 mana is the clearest discard since it won't be cast any time soon.

annotations.description: Discarding Psychic Frog is a significant mistake. Psychic Frog is a 2-mana creature that synergizes extremely well with the discard-heavy gameplan, can grow with +1/+1 counters by discarding cards, gains flying, and draws cards on combat damage. With only 2 lands in play (Steam Vents and Island), Llama4 Timmy needs cheap, impactful plays. Psychic Frog at UB is castable next turn with a Bloodstained Mire fetch. Meanwhile, Archon of Cruelty at 6BB is completely uncastable for many turns and could have been discarded instead - it's a reanimation target but there's no reanimation spell in hand or evident in the deck. Discarding Archon of Cruelty (as a potential future reanimation target that's dead in hand) alongside Emperor of Bones would have been better, keeping both Psychic Frogs as the primary game plan with 2 lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Psychic Frog as the second card to Faithless Looting (alongside Emperor of Bones)
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty instead of Psychic Frog. Archon costs 8 mana and is uncastable for many turns, while Psychic Frog is a key 2-mana threat that can be deployed immediately and synergizes with the discard gameplan.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge had the infinite combo available: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf. Young Wolf then gains Walking Ballista's 'remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability. Removing the counter kills Young Wolf, undying returns it with a +1/+1 counter, and the loop repeats for infinite damage — killing the opponent at 10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Appears to have dismissed activating Agatha's Soul Cauldron and likely cast Walking Ballista from hand instead, missing the infinite combo.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in graveyard, put +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf, then loop: remove counter from Young Wolf to deal 1 damage, Young Wolf dies and returns via undying with a +1/+1 counter. Repeat for lethal.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from a graveyard (Llama4 Timmy's graveyard has no Walking Ballista, but their own graveyard has one). Exiling Walking Ballista with Agatha's Soul Cauldron is a key combo piece - it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal damage, and Walking Ballista's activated abilities. With Young Wolf (which has undying and can get +1/+1 counters) on the battlefield, this creates a powerful synergy. The Walking Ballista is on the stack resolving, but there's also one in Sarge's own graveyard that could be exiled with the Cauldron. Declining this activation wastes a critical combo opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron, passing priority while Walking Ballista was on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the graveyard to exile it and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf), giving that creature Walking Ballista's activated abilities for a powerful damage engine.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from the opponent's graveyard. Walking Ballista is one of the most powerful cards to exile with Agatha's Soul Cauldron, as it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal 1 damage to any target. Young Wolf with undying gets a +1/+1 counter when it returns, and the Cauldron itself can put +1/+1 counters on creatures by exiling creature cards. Exiling Walking Ballista with the Cauldron would enable a powerful combo engine where any creature with a +1/+1 counter becomes a damage source. The player's reasoning was confused, claiming the activation wasn't relevant, but this is actually a key synergy in their deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron, passing priority and moving toward combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the opponent's graveyard to exile it and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature (like Young Wolf). This enables the Walking Ballista activated ability on all creatures with +1/+1 counters, creating a powerful damage engine.

annotations.description: Fetched Watery Grave instead of basic Swamp when already having an Island for blue mana. At 9 life against an aggressive board, the 2 life payment for Watery Grave is unnecessary since a basic Swamp provides the needed black mana without any life cost while Island already covers blue.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Watery Grave (will cost 2 life to enter untapped or enter tapped)
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Swamp - provides the needed black mana for Thoughtseize, Psychic Frog, Emperor of Bones, and Bitter Triumph without any life cost, since Island already provides blue mana.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from their own graveyard. Exiling Walking Ballista with the Cauldron would grant its 'remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability to all creatures with +1/+1 counters. This synergizes with Young Wolf's undying (returns with a +1/+1 counter), creating a recurring ping source. The player also incorrectly claimed they had no black mana for Spymaster's Vault when Underground Mortuary was available (though connive for 0 would have been useless).
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either ability, passing priority with Walking Ballista on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in their own graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf or another creature, and granting the Ballista ping ability to creatures with counters.

annotations.description: Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron while there was a Walking Ballista in their graveyard. Exiling Walking Ballista with Soul Cauldron would put a +1/+1 counter on a creature and grant it Walking Ballista's activated abilities (including the ability to remove +1/+1 counters to deal damage). With the opponent at 4 life, this is extremely relevant - any creature with +1/+1 counters could gain the ability to shoot the opponent. The Walking Ballista was also on the stack (being cast by opponent via Bitter Triumph interaction), but the copy in Sarge's graveyard could have been exiled to set up the Ballista ability on creatures with counters. Additionally, Young Wolf with undying would be a perfect target since it comes back with a +1/+1 counter and would then have Ballista's ping ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron, passing priority and letting the stack resolve without interaction.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron targeting Walking Ballista in the graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on a creature (ideally Young Wolf or another creature). This would grant that creature Walking Ballista's activated abilities, potentially enabling a kill on the opponent at 4 life through ping damage, especially combined with Young Wolf's undying mechanic.

annotations.description: Spent 4 mana to put a +1/+1 counter on a creature via Walking Ballista's ability when Agatha's Soul Cauldron's tap ability could exile a creature card from a graveyard (opponent has Emperor of Bones, Psychic Frog in graveyard) and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature for free. This wastes mana that could have been used for additional counters or other plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista's {4}: Put a +1/+1 counter ability, spending 4 mana for one counter.
annotations.betterLine: First activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile a creature card from a graveyard (getting a free +1/+1 counter), then use remaining mana for the {4} Walking Ballista ability if possible, maximizing counters and thus damage potential toward the opponent at 4 life.

annotations.description: With opponent at 4 life and all lands tapped, Sarge should first use Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile a creature card from a graveyard to add another +1/+1 counter to their creature, maximizing Walking Ballista pings to 3 damage, then attack with Young Wolf for the 4th point of lethal damage. By removing a Ballista counter first, they reduce their total damage potential and may miss the exact lethal line.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista's remove-counter ability first, reducing available counters before using Cauldron to potentially add more.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron first to exile a creature card (e.g., Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog from opponent's graveyard) and put a +1/+1 counter on the creature with Ballista abilities, then remove all 3 counters for 3 damage, then attack with Young Wolf for exactly 4 lethal damage.

annotations.description: Removing a +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to the opponent at 4 life is unnecessary when attacking with Young Wolf (1/1) + Badgermole Cub (2/2) + Walking Ballista (2/2) = 5 damage is already lethal. annotations.betterLine: Skip the Ballista activation and simply attack with Young Wolf, Badgermole Cub, and Walking Ballista for 5 total damage against an opponent at 4 life with no blockers and all lands tapped, preserving the extra counter.

annotations.description: Opponent was at 4 life with no blockers and all lands tapped. After pinging with Walking Ballista to bring opponent to 3, Sarge skipped the attack phase entirely. Young Wolf (1/1) + Badgermole Cub (2/2) = 3 damage = exactly lethal. Alternatively, attacking with all creatures before pinging would have dealt 4+ damage for lethal without needing the Ballista activation.
annotations.actionTaken: Pinged opponent with Walking Ballista for 1 damage (opponent to 3 life) then skipped the attack phase.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Young Wolf and Badgermole Cub (and any other available attackers) for lethal damage. The opponent at 3 life with no blockers and no mana available cannot survive 3+ damage from attackers.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Abhorrent Oculus (exiling all 6 graveyard cards) to get a 5/5 flyer, stabilizing the board at 3 life with a dominant threat and blocker

annotations.actionTaken: Removed the last +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to Llama4 Timmy pre-combat, killing the Ballista.
annotations.betterLine: Skip the Ballista activation and just attack with available creatures for lethal. Keep Walking Ballista alive as a 1/1 body in case something goes wrong, or save the counter for potential future use.
